one_sentence: Kilian (2009, American Economic Review) develops a structural VAR to disentangle oil supply shocks, aggregate demand shocks, and oil-market-specific demand shocks in the crude oil market and traces their differing effects on the real price of oil and the US economy.

issues.original: Year = {2009} (appears on line 7 and again on line 11)
issues.reason: Duplicated field key in the same @article block. BibTeX entries must not repeat a field name; most parsers silently keep one value (implementation-dependent) rather than erroring, which is fragile hygiene even though the duplicated value happened to be identical and non-contradictory here.

issues.original: Month = {June} (appears on line 8 and again on line 10)
issues.reason: Same duplicated-field problem as Year. Both duplicates carried the same value, so no factual error resulted, but the entry should be de-duplicated for BibTeX hygiene.

The original uses a literal Unicode en-dash (U+2013) character inside the .bib source. BibTeX/BibLaTeX convention is to encode a page-range dash as ASCII double-hyphen (--), which .bst styles render as an en-dash at typeset time; a raw Unicode en-dash can break under non-UTF8 BibTeX toolchains or render inconsistently. Also expanded the truncated '69' to the full '1069' to avoid ambiguity, though the AEA's own abbreviated '1053–69' is not itself wrong.
No DOI field was present. Adding it is standard hygiene for a published journal article and gives a durable canonical anchor; confirmed against the AEA article landing page.
